title: Vectors in databases you already use: Supabase and MongoDB Atlas

videos.script: Marginalia already runs PostgreSQL. Its orders, its accounts and its help articles all live there. {{tables}} The last two lessons met stores built for vectors and little else. This one asks a cheaper question first. Can the database you already have do the job? {{extension}} For PostgreSQL the answer is an extension called pgvector. It adds a column type, three distance operators and two kinds of index. {{search}} You will store the help centre in a table and search it with one SQL query. Then you will score all twenty-four test questions in a single statement, by joining two tables. {{plan}} You will add an index and watch the query plan change. You will also watch an index quietly lose two of three results. {{hosted}} Then two hosted services. Supabase is PostgreSQL with pgvector, reached over the web. MongoDB Atlas keeps the vector inside a document and searches it in an aggregation pipeline. Neither is reachable from this machine, so their code is shown and not run. {{choice}} Last, the question that decides it. When is one database enough, and when does it stop being enough? {{end}}
